long_biography.plain_text:
Mauricio Amodio's work at Papalote Museo del Niño has involved both expanding a museum and keeping its teaching available when visitors could not enter. As board chairman, he helped lead the Chapultepec museum's renovation, which enlarged the building and garden and renewed its interactive exhibits. He emphasised improved visitor facilities and more responsible use of natural resources.

When the pandemic closed the museums in 2020, Amodio and director Dolores Beistegui faced the loss of operating income. The institution launched Papalote en Casa, providing educational activities for children, families and teachers online. Its marketing and experience-design teams built the platform, while management and the board reduced expenditure to sustain the institution.
